[[Category:Probability]]
'''Conditional probability''' is the probability of one event given another event.

== Definition ==

{{#content:Q2941}}

<ref>{{#cite:Q2940}}</ref>

== Multiplication law ==

By rearrangement of terms of definition, 

$$
P(A \cap B) = P(A\ |\ B) P(B) = P(B\ |\ A) P(A)
$$

<blockquote>
Note 
$$
P(A\cap B)\equiv P(B\cap A)\\
P(A\ |\ B)\neq P(B\ |\ A).
$$
</blockquote>

== Bayes law ==

$$
P(B\ |\ A) = \frac{P(A\ |\ B) P(B)}{P(A)}.\notag
$$

as a direct result of [[#Multiplication law]].

== Partition law ==

If

* $S = B_1 \cup B_2 \cup \cdots \cup B_n$,
* $\forall i \neq j: B_i\cap B_j = \varnothing$,
* $\forall i \in 1,\cdots ,n P(B_i)>0$,

Then

$$
P(A|S) = P(A\ |\ B_1) P(B_1) + \cdots + P(A\ |\ B_n) P(B_n).\notag
$$

and $B_1, B_2, \ldots, B_n$ are said to '''partition''' sample space $S$.

<ref>{{#cite:Q2940}}</ref>

== Application ==

=== Medical screening accuracy ===

Consider a kidney cancer screening test, which

* correctly detects when a person has cancer 90% of the time
* correctly indicates when a person does not have kidney cancer 99.9% of the time

Suppose it is known that 1 in every 10,000 individuals has kidney cancer. 

What is the probability that a patient has kidney cancer, given a positive test result?
